flags: Caltrans spreadsheet 00.txt is unreadable binary-like text. Official designation and generic program language are quoted through 01.txt; the specific designation date is unverified.
The cache contains no road construction chronology or detailed grades, curves or driving duration; the overview uses the documented dam-settlement history and limited driving description.
The whole numbered route and mapped corridor continue east beyond the scenic segment ending at Lake Boulevard.

Dam closure wording is retained from 01.txt, but no current Bureau of Reclamation access notice is cached. The requested checked date denotes cache review only. Tours and elevator access are omitted because no current manager source verifies them.

The current claim that Kennett flooded within five years of groundbreaking conflicts with 02.txt’s September 1937 ceremony and February 1944 storage dates. The Kennett article also gives a conflicting 1935 construction start; omitted precise inundation timing.
Winnemem Wintu history is supported only by a secondary cache page; no tribal source is available. Do not reuse the source’s dismissive description of the living tribe.
Toyon has no dedicated Wikipedia coordinates line in this cache; its new moment is unpinned. The fenced site is not presented as open for entry.
The current overview’s “little over three miles” distance is absent from readable cache evidence and has been dropped.
